ESPLE-DP-P1.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: The family consists of products whose shared domain assumptions warrant coordinated production; code resemblance alone is insufficient.
ESPLE-DP-P1.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Commonality must survive comparison of actual needs; variation includes intended alternatives, not every historical difference.
ESPLE-DP-P1.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Features are statements about product needs before they become selectable variables; scope precedes formal completeness.
ESPLE-DP-P1.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: No binding time is prescribed by scoping; the cost and feasibility of possible binding choices constrain what the family can promise.
ESPLE-DP-P1.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Only assets with a defensible cross-product consumer belong in the shared investment case.
ESPLE-DP-P1.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Scope identifies which derived products the family claims to support; precise baseline identity is established by the production model.
ESPLE-DP-P1.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Broader scope can add interactions; scoping alone supplies no coverage or correctness result.
ESPLE-DP-P1.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Changed demand or incompatible product assumptions can require a split, migration or end of shared production.
ESPLE-DP-P1.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Affected product stakeholders must be represented; legitimate exceptions can invalidate a too-broad common-core assumption.
ESPLE-DP-P1.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Expected reuse, coordination and support cost must be compared with independent products or selective component reuse.

ESPLE-DP-P2.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Domain and application work are justified by a family whose reusable capabilities serve actual or credible products.
ESPLE-DP-P2.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: The common core and product-local work are related but not identical; repeated local differences require examination, not automatic generalisation.
ESPLE-DP-P2.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Product requests can expose absent or mistaken features and constraints; feedback may change the model or preserve an exception.
ESPLE-DP-P2.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Shared and local decisions can bind at different stages; adoption strategy must not predetermine all technical binding choices.
ESPLE-DP-P2.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Domain work maintains reusable assets; application work derives products and returns feasibility and failure evidence.
ESPLE-DP-P2.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Product observations need enough baseline and configuration identity to be actionable across the family.
ESPLE-DP-P2.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Local success does not prove safe generalisation; shared repairs need product-impact analysis.
ESPLE-DP-P2.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Feedback is recurrent and can interrupt planned development; extractive, reactive and proactive routes can coexist over time.
ESPLE-DP-P2.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: The same people may hold both responsibilities; exceptions retain support accountability and limits on inherited guarantees.
ESPLE-DP-P2.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Coordination and asset preparation are real costs; a small shared capability or continued cloning can dominate full platform adoption.

ESPLE-DP-P3.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: The model represents a declared product family, not every conceivable configuration in the technology domain.
ESPLE-DP-P3.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Common and variable characteristics are explicit semantic decisions; historical product observations do not exhaust valid possibilities.
ESPLE-DP-P3.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Boolean, cardinality, attribute and typed constraints describe encoded validity; domain adequacy must be checked outside solver consistency.
ESPLE-DP-P3.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: A model choice may bind before build, at deployment or at runtime; selection semantics do not determine realisation timing by themselves.
ESPLE-DP-P3.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Features relate to requirements and assets through possibly many-to-many mappings; neither a node nor a flag is automatically a module.
ESPLE-DP-P3.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: A configuration identifies model selections under a particular model version; it is not yet the identity of a built product.
ESPLE-DP-P3.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Constraint analysis excludes some invalid combinations but does not establish implementation interactions or input coverage.
ESPLE-DP-P3.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Model edits can add or remove products; feature correspondence and changed meaning must be considered during migration.
ESPLE-DP-P3.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Experts validate domain intent and configurators make product decisions within authorised bounds; models can be decentralised if composition is checked.
ESPLE-DP-P3.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Use the least costly representation that preserves consequential distinctions; a decision table or direct guidance can be adequate.

ESPLE-DP-P4.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Realisation choices serve the selected family scope rather than requiring all products to share one implementation technique.
ESPLE-DP-P4.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Shared code, product-specific code and interaction glue may coexist; arbitrary duplication is neither automatically valuable nor forbidden.
ESPLE-DP-P4.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Selection-to-implementation relations must preserve feature meaning; syntactic modularity alone does not establish semantic alignment.
ESPLE-DP-P4.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Compile, deployment and runtime binding carry different footprint, timing and transition obligations; later is not universally better.
ESPLE-DP-P4.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Assets may be annotated, composed, parameterised or transformed; the core need not be one monolithic source tree.
ESPLE-DP-P4.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Generator, template, build and dependency versions can affect the realised variant and belong in relevant provenance.
ESPLE-DP-P4.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Cross-mechanism interactions require checks; successful code generation or compilation is not product correctness.
ESPLE-DP-P4.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Changes to realisation or binding time can invalidate mappings, supported configurations and previous assurance.
ESPLE-DP-P4.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Implementers choose within family obligations; product-local exceptions require explicit support and do not inherit all shared claims.
ESPLE-DP-P4.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Technique complexity must be earned by demand and assurance needs; ordinary parameters, modules or manual derivation remain alternatives.

ESPLE-DP-P5.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Core assets and production plans are bounded by the supported family and its product obligations.
ESPLE-DP-P5.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Common assets include consumed non-code knowledge; variability is intentional in both artefacts and production decisions.
ESPLE-DP-P5.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: A product configuration has meaning only with feature semantics and compatible realisation inputs.
ESPLE-DP-P5.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Production records identify where consequential choices are resolved; runtime variability remains an additional product obligation.
ESPLE-DP-P5.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Requirements, architecture, code, tests, documentation and tools are core assets only where products actually use them.
ESPLE-DP-P5.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Product identity joins configuration, relevant asset/tool versions and realised outputs; required repeatability must name its equivalence level.
ESPLE-DP-P5.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Derivation provenance supports diagnosis and evidence transfer but does not establish feature-interaction correctness.
ESPLE-DP-P5.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Old products may depend on older tools and assets; current-mainline availability is not a substitute for support continuity.
ESPLE-DP-P5.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Builders execute production plans; asset maintainers own changes and product authorities accept results or exceptions.
ESPLE-DP-P5.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Automation and provenance detail are proportionate to volume, risk and support; a short checked manual procedure can suffice.

ESPLE-DP-P6.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Assurance quantifies over a declared configuration set, not an undefined claim about every possible product.
ESPLE-DP-P6.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Sharing analysis requires common semantics and represented variability; shared defects and omitted assumptions can affect many variants.
ESPLE-DP-P6.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Model validity, implementation well-formedness and behavioural correctness are distinct claims and need explicit connecting premises.
ESPLE-DP-P6.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Compile-time selection, build layers and runtime transitions change the space that an assurance method must cover.
ESPLE-DP-P6.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Reusable tests, contracts and conditional results can support several products only while their assumptions remain true.
ESPLE-DP-P6.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Evidence must identify the model, code, tool and product baseline to which it applies.
ESPLE-DP-P6.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Coverage includes configurations, interactions, inputs and environments; pairwise feature coverage is not complete behavioural coverage.
ESPLE-DP-P6.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Changed constraints or shared assets can invalidate samples, contracts, test oracles and inherited results.
ESPLE-DP-P6.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Analysts provide evidence; product acceptance and risk decisions remain with authorised consumers, including product-specific exceptions.
ESPLE-DP-P6.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Choose product, feature, family or hybrid checking by claim, scale and cost; exhaustive analysis may be cheaper for a small supported set.

ESPLE-DP-P7.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Evolution preserves or explicitly revises obligations of supported products, not just the newest family model.
ESPLE-DP-P7.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Some variation remains valuable only for legacy support; recovery from products must distinguish history from desired future scope.
ESPLE-DP-P7.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Feature names and model syntax can change without semantic change, and stable names can conceal changed intent.
ESPLE-DP-P7.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Migration can change binding or traverse intermediate configurations; live transitions require the separate dynamic model.
ESPLE-DP-P7.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Changes may affect code, tests, requirements, generators, interfaces and production plans together.
ESPLE-DP-P7.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Old and new product identities and compatibility relations must remain distinguishable during migration or parallel support.
ESPLE-DP-P7.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Regression work targets affected variants and assumptions; model-set preservation alone does not establish behaviour preservation.
ESPLE-DP-P7.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Migration, deprecation, test repair and retirement have different consumers and triggers; support-aware retirement need not retain new-product admission.
ESPLE-DP-P7.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Core and product maintainers coordinate fixes; a shared change cannot silently override an exceptional product obligation.
ESPLE-DP-P7.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Retaining multiple baselines has costs, but premature consolidation can break products; cloning or deferred migration can be the adequate alternative.

ESPLE-DP-P8.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Family scope and expected product demand are assumptions in the economic case, not benefits created by writing a model.
ESPLE-DP-P8.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Reuse frequency and stable commonality determine whether shared investment can pay; uncertainty must remain visible.
ESPLE-DP-P8.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Feature-space size can estimate effort but is not equivalent to customer value or realised product demand.
ESPLE-DP-P8.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Binding choices shift cost between preparation, builds, deployment and runtime operation.
ESPLE-DP-P8.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Asset investment includes requirements, implementation, production tools, assurance and ongoing coordination, not just reusable code.
ESPLE-DP-P8.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Comparable alternatives need equivalent product and support outcomes; configuration identity supports measuring actual work rather than counting labels.
ESPLE-DP-P8.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Assurance cost and consequences of shared defects belong in the comparison; cheaper development is not adequate if mandatory outcomes fail.
ESPLE-DP-P8.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Maintenance, migration, deprecation and exit costs matter over the selected horizon; sunk costs do not settle prospective decisions.
ESPLE-DP-P8.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Shared benefits and costs fall on different teams; incentives and product autonomy affect whether nominal savings materialise.
ESPLE-DP-P8.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Independent development, selective reuse, modular single products and clone-and-own are legitimate comparators; no universal break-even count is retained.

ESPLE-DP-P9.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Organisational reach and participant autonomy bound the family; an ecosystem may not be one controlled product line.
ESPLE-DP-P9.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: Sharing can concern code, specifications or interfaces; those forms create different control and compatibility relationships.
ESPLE-DP-P9.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Features can encode customer or external constraints, but their legal/security applicability must come from competent external evidence.
ESPLE-DP-P9.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Authority to bind or rebind a choice is separate from its representability in a model.
ESPLE-DP-P9.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Core assets have maintainers and consumers; externally owned components and autonomous derivatives are not silently internal assets.
ESPLE-DP-P9.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Product and asset provenance supports accountability without granting ownership over external participants.
ESPLE-DP-P9.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: A common core can create common-mode exposure; external compatibility and product-specific obligations remain part of assurance.
ESPLE-DP-P9.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Independent release schedules, suppliers and support commitments constrain shared changes and retirement.
ESPLE-DP-P9.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Contribution, variation, exception and release authority must be explicit and proportionate; a committee is not universally required.
ESPLE-DP-P9.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Coordination, training and bottlenecks are costs; simpler ownership or ordinary dependency management can be adequate where no family governance is needed.

ESPLE-DP-P10.FAMILY_SCOPE_AND_EXPECTED_REUSE: Dynamic and AI-assisted variants remain bounded by a declared family; broader ecosystem derivatives may require a different organisational model.
ESPLE-DP-P10.COMMONALITY_AND_VARIABILITY_ASSUMPTIONS: A permitted set of alternatives is not permission to change arbitrarily; learned suggestions do not establish new valid commonality.
ESPLE-DP-P10.FEATURE_SEMANTICS_AND_CONSTRAINTS: Static configuration constraints, runtime requirements and learned proposal validity must be distinguished.
ESPLE-DP-P10.VARIATION_POINT_AND_BINDING_TIME: Runtime rebinding introduces transition paths, state continuity and actual controllability; fixed features do not imply environment-independent execution.
ESPLE-DP-P10.CORE_ASSET_AND_PRODUCT_RELATION: Models, controllers, generators and validation assets participate in derivation, but each has a separate realisation and maintenance burden.
ESPLE-DP-P10.DERIVATION_AND_CONFIGURATION_IDENTITY: Observed runtime state and generated output need identity distinct from the requested configuration or prompt.
ESPLE-DP-P10.FEATURE_INTERACTION_AND_COVERAGE_BOUNDAR: Safe endpoints do not establish safe transitions; proofs require adequate plant models and generated outputs require independent validation.
ESPLE-DP-P10.EVOLUTION_AND_MIGRATION_OBLIGATIONS: Model and tool changes can invalidate runtime policies or regenerated variants; continuity must be checked rather than presumed.
ESPLE-DP-P10.OWNERSHIP_AND_PRODUCT_EXCEPTION_POLICY: Operators and accountable product authorities authorise actions; formal models and learned assistants possess no self-created operational authority.
ESPLE-DP-P10.ECONOMIC_ASSUMPTIONS_AND_NON_PRODUCT_LIN: Offline selection, deterministic transformations or no adaptation may dominate runtime/AI machinery when their extra capability has no justified consumer.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S007 motivation/scoping; S041 Sections 2, 4–6
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Precise family models can formalise the wrong scope; too-broad commonality makes unrelated products pay for each other.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: PuLSE explicitly responds to impractical domain-engineering scope. Bosch reports mixed dependencies across selected products and the inadequacy of one stale global model.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Product-focused scope and subsystem-aligned models narrow the coordination boundary; neither requires erasing common knowledge.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain warranted scope, reject vocabulary or code duplication as sufficient family evidence. Split or narrow when assumptions conflict.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No universal similarity measure predicts useful family scope or future demand.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S010 introduction/Section 4; S012 economic scenarios; S013 failure discussion
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Upfront platform investment can outrun uncertain demand and consume resources before any payoff.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Adoption methods explicitly propose reactive/extractive alternatives; SIMPLE makes returns depend on multiple cost terms rather than a universal product count.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Choose a staged route or no product-line transition when the business and asset conditions do not justify anticipation.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain strategy selection and sensitivity analysis; reject compulsory full upfront platforms and universal break-even numbers.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Forecast error and unreported failed programmes prevent a general probability of success.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S026 study design/results; S027 experiment and validity; S028 institutional abstract
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Shared production can cost more than locally independent variants; cloning is not necessarily careless engineering.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Qualitative industrial accounts describe autonomy and startup advantages. A small BSH task comparison favours SPLE in its setting, while later debt evidence describes unsynchronised-asset burdens.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Use a lifecycle and obligation-matched comparison; bounded exceptions or selective reuse can preserve autonomy without losing all provenance.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Reject anti-cloning universality, but do not infer lifetime cloning superiority from practitioners explaining why they use it.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Matched longitudinal portfolio comparisons including transition and exit costs remain scarce in the inspected corpus.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S005 Section 7.3.2; S015 analysis-operation discussion; S041 Sections 2, 3.5
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Models and traces can become elaborate but unused documentation.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Original FODA includes rationale and dependency information; Bosch reports central models falling out of use and a tension between simplified formulas and traceability to code.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Require a real configuration, derivation or impact consumer; align representation and ownership with maintained assets.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain semantics and needed traceability; feature-tree presence is ceremony, not fulfilment.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: The minimum useful representation varies with team knowledge and interaction scale.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S014 logic encoding; S041 Section 6 construct validity
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A consistent or reverse-engineered constraint set can permit products that make no sense in the domain.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The Bosch case explicitly distinguishes feature-effect constraints from complete domain knowledge and describes omitted artefact types and approximations.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Use independent positive/negative domain cases and expert review; keep encoded validity separate from domain and implementation validity.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Strong formal consistency survives, while claims of comprehensive validity are narrowed.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No finite example set establishes complete domain knowledge without further assumptions.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S017 Sections 4.3–4.4; S018 delta construction; S041 Section 2
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Neither annotation nor feature modularity universally avoids scattering, interaction glue and coordination problems.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: FOSD discusses complementary implementation mechanisms; deltas add removals/changes; Bosch combines component selection and conditional compilation.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Select mechanisms by granularity, binding time and change needs; expose many-to-many realisation and ordering obligations.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain a portfolio; do not prescribe one feature/one module or replace every conditional with specialised machinery.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Comparative lifecycle benefits of mixed realisation remain highly setting-dependent.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S021 Sections 5–7 and results for version 3.6.1
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Configuration validity does not ensure a working generated stack.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The bounded JHipster study reports thousands of failing valid configurations associated with a small number of interaction faults; the text contains a one-configuration count discrepancy.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Separate model, generation/build and product-behaviour claims; preserve failing configuration and baseline identity.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Reject SAT-to-product correctness. The empirical result demonstrates possibility and materiality in one version, not current prevalence.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No universal failure rate follows from a single generator or its historical test workflow.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S020 RQ1–RQ3; S021 sampling comparison; S040 validity discussion
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Pairwise coverage misses higher-order or non-configuration faults, and sampling rankings depend on realistic cost and extraction assumptions.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Sampling comparisons and exhaustive bounded testing expose different trade-offs. Variability-aware static analysis compares warnings, not adjudicated bug incidence.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Select by claim and budget; add risk-directed checks or family analysis when supported. Report actual costs and residual coverage.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain sampling conditionally; reject completeness claims and warnings-as-fault-prevalence.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Risk distributions in future products and omitted environments are not known from these benchmarks.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S019 strategy assumptions; S031 Sections 4–8; S040 printed p. 26; S041 Section 6
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A sound analysis of an incomplete representation gives false confidence about an implementation or physical environment.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Missing build layers, approximate extraction, pointer-analysis limits and modelled controllability constrain transfer.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Keep the theorem or analysis result, but expose and check representation and implementation obligations separately.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Strong internal validity is compatible with weak deployment evidence; do not weaken the theorem or exaggerate its reach.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Model adequacy is an engineering evidence burden, not supplied by syntactic proof completion.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S023 semantic edit classification; S024 migration model; S037 Sections 6–9
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Preserved configuration sets or minimal selection changes do not prove preserved product intent, behaviour or maintenance effort.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Model comparison and migration algorithms operate on declared representations. Test-evolution research acknowledges that configuration distance may not represent real editing effort.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Add explicit feature correspondence and product acceptance; choose regression and novelty-oriented test objectives deliberately.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain model-level methods with bounded claims; reject behavioural compatibility inferred from names or set equality.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Real-world effort and higher-order evolution need more direct evidence.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S027 participant design, tasks, results and validity discussion
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A short industrial task experiment is not a causal estimate of whole-programme SPLE return.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Ten engineers each perform four tasks: forty task observations are clustered within people, not forty independent engineers. Platform preparation and migration investment are not measured.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Treat the observed task comparison as local evidence. Our methodological caution does not reanalyse unavailable raw data or claim a published correction.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain the local favourable finding, reject its use as a universal payoff or independent-sample denominator.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: A robust longitudinal comparison would measure repeated changes, preparation, support and participant clustering.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S013 experience/failure discussion; S026 industrial findings; S028 abstract; S041 Section 2
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Central asset ownership can create bottlenecks and misaligned incentives while product teams carry delivery obligations.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Failures and practical variation strategies reveal organisational constraints not solved by code reuse or tool deployment.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Make decision rights and resources explicit; decentralise where responsibilities and model composition support it; permit bounded exceptions.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain accountable shared decisions, not a universal central team or committee.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: There is no evidence here for a universally optimal team topology or meeting frequency.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S030 discussion of safe/quiescent reconfiguration; S031 Sections 4–7
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Valid endpoints can be joined by unsafe transitions, and a modelled atomic action may not be realisable.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Early dynamic work leaves transition safety open; supervisory-control work explicitly models events and requirements.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Check path/state continuity, actual controllability and safe reconfiguration phases; prefer offline selection when live operation cannot be justified.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Transition safety is strongly retained when live rebinding occurs; runtime flexibility is not universally preferred.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Sensor accuracy, timing and physical actuation may remain outside the analysed model.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S031 Section 8 and model-assumption discussion
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: An industrial-origin benchmark is mistaken for deployment evidence or safety certification.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The Body Comfort System demonstrates model construction and synthesis, not a reported operational vehicle deployment.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Preserve the formal result and bounded case scale, while requiring separate model/plant and operational evidence.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Supervisory control remains domain-specific; nonblocking is not inevitable progress on all executions.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Independent deployment validation and behaviour under model mismatch are not established here.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S032 language levels and discussion; S033 public scope
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A shared syntax or a specialised standard is universalised into semantic interoperability or a definition of all SPLE.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: UVL has defined expressive levels and tool boundaries. The ISO public scope calls feature-based PLE a specialisation of a broader reference model.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Check supported versions/semantics and state the narrow normative scope actually inspected.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain checked interchange; reject total automation as a universal field definition.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Unseen normative clauses and the legal history of earlier language initiatives are not inferred.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S034 exploratory study/limitations; S036 access-limited record; S038 design/results
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Plausible learned changes or small examples are promoted into reliable autonomous product-family evolution.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The inspected regeneration proposal is exploratory; adjacent DSL evaluation exposes scale/complexity limits. A direct SPLC co-evolution paper and later regeneration version remain access-limited.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Use learned output as a proposal with independent validation and matched deterministic/manual alternatives.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain bounded assistance as assumption-sensitive; leave replacement superiority unresolved rather than adopt or dismiss it without evidence.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Repeated-change continuity, unseen-version results and full lifecycle comparisons could change the replacement judgement.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S041 legacy-variability treatment; S045 Sections 5.4, 7 and 8
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: More variability is treated as progress; removal is treated as harmless because current products rarely use an option.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Legacy variation can remain needed for old products, while smaller programs also demonstrate that options can be bound earlier or removed.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Separate admission to new products from existing support; keep usage uncertainty and migration costs explicit.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain support-aware retirement, not maximal variability or automatic deletion of low-frequency options.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Observed use can miss rare but consequential requirements; code-size correlations do not establish causal maintenance savings.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S029 organisational boundary; S044 Sections 1, 4–5
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A shared ecosystem specification is assumed to imply a centrally managed core and enforceable product derivation.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Community-driven variability distinguishes autonomous proposal/implementation evolution from classical product-line production.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Keep ecosystem interfaces and documentary intersections, but do not impose internal SPLE control over independent participants.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Preserve a conditional external interface; full unification with autonomous ecosystems is not established.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Taxonomy and classification do not demonstrate effective governance or the payoff of proposed feature-oriented tooling.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: Cross-source programme/dataset metadata in source table and empirical register
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Repeated papers or reports about the same industrial programme or benchmark are counted as independent replication.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: SEI/Lucent experience, TypeChef/configurable-C subjects, BCS and repeated observations within studies create evidence dependence.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Record programme and dataset clusters and distinguish units, organisations, products, tasks and model runs.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: No aggregate confidence percentage or pooled causal effect is computed.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: Complete overlap cannot be established for inaccessible datasets; possible overlap is retained as uncertainty.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: Access levels and claim locators in source table
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Bibliographic discovery or abstract access is presented as full reconstruction of methodology, clauses or empirical outcomes.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Several canonical works, normative text and recent publications were accessible only in part despite lawful alternate attempts.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Use separate inspected primary works for mechanisms; retain the limited work only for supported history or problem scope.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Examination may be complete within an explicit evidence limit without inventing the missing content.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: These access limits bound historical detail and particular modern results; they are not negative findings about the works.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S045 Sections 7.2 P3, 7.3 and 8
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Early binding of all selectable features is used to infer context-independent behaviour.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: The proposal also allows non-identical outputs; its broad wording is not a proof that ordinary inputs, state or environment have no effect.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Retain fixed configurability as a useful distinction; separately model ordinary execution and environmental assumptions.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Reject the stronger implication with an analytical counterexample, without attributing a claim of identical output for every input to the authors.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: A narrower formal semantics could clarify the intended behavioural consistency; it would not establish arbitrary environmental robustness.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S011 production-plan development and version management; S021 Results/Discussion; S041 Sections 3–6
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A complete-looking asset inventory, architecture document or automated build can remain disconnected from the actually produced product.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Production-plan guidance names the assets and production relationships; configurable-generator and reverse-engineering studies expose realisation and heterogeneous-artefact limits.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Retain only consequential asset and tool identity, make the plan consumable by derivation, define repeatability equivalence and test outputs independently.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Retain production control, not maximal documentation or universal byte-for-byte build identity. This is a synthesis of distinct evidence, not a reported comparative trial of provenance policies.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: The least costly sufficient provenance and architecture enforcement depend on the failure consequences and actual build environment.

criticism_ledger.CLAIM_LOCATOR: S011 version management; S026 findings on propagation; S029 organisational expansion; S041 Section 3 legacy/commonality discussion
criticism_ledger.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Uniform propagation and forced simplification can violate the obligations of a supported product; preserving every exception can in turn destroy the economics of sharing.
criticism_ledger.EVIDENCE: Industrial cloning and Bosch observations show heterogeneous product obligations and propagation/support difficulties; ecosystem work separates organisational authorities.
criticism_ledger.RESPONSE_AND_LATER_FINDINGS: Coordinate impact, preserve identified support baselines where justified, and explicitly decide differentiated repair or retirement with those responsible for the product.
criticism_ledger.PRESENT_JUDGEMENT: Support and external obligations constrain core change, but no source establishes an unlimited duty to maintain every variant indefinitely. Exact legal or contractual content remains an external input.
criticism_ledger.RESIDUAL_UNCERTAINTY: No universal exception budget or support duration follows from this tradition.

ceremony_stripping_ledger.ARTEFACT_RITUAL_OR_BRAND: Portfolio similarity matrix or domain-scoping workshop
ceremony_stripping_ledger.FAILURE: Superficially similar products can require incompatible assumptions, release obligations or ownership arrangements.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.CONSUMER: Portfolio and domain decision-makers with product representatives; similarity analysis does not authorise merging teams or obligations.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.PREREQUISITES: Product needs, differences, expected future use and who can sustain shared assets.

ceremony_stripping_ledger.ARTEFACT_RITUAL_OR_BRAND: Runtime adaptation framework, interoperable model or learned assistant
ceremony_stripping_ledger.FAILURE: An adaptation design assumes it may change components, users' choices or physical actuators merely because the model allows it.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.CONSUMER: Operators and accountable product authorities decide deployment; the proof author cannot create authority through notation.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.PREREQUISITES: Model/plant mapping, permissions, controllability and operational feedback.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Keep the result advisory or use an existing authorised operational process when actuation is not established.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: A formal or generated controller is proposed for real runtime configuration.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Simplification is inadequate if it loses this consequential postcondition: Each real action is feasible and authorised, and the observed consequence is checked separately from the command being issued.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_FULLER_FORM: Validation and operational coordination; ignoring the boundary can create unauthorised or unsafe change.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Remove the unsupported inference; retain valid model analysis as evidence or advice.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION based on the source-grounded property, not a separately evaluated ceremony-removal intervention.

ceremony_stripping_ledger.ARTEFACT_RITUAL_OR_BRAND: Migration plan, change-control board and recovery model
ceremony_stripping_ledger.FAILURE: Obsolete options burden new derivation, but indiscriminate removal destroys the ability to maintain older variants.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.CONSUMER: Product support and core maintainers agree retirement; apparent non-use in a sample is not permission to abandon a supported customer.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.PREREQUISITES: Actual usage, supported products, external commitments and the effect of removal on derivation and tests.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: Mark the feature unavailable to new configurations while retaining the older baseline, rather than immediately rewriting all code.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: A feature is unused for new demand, fixed to one value or becomes disproportionately costly to support.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Simplification is inadequate if it loses this consequential postcondition: New products no longer inherit unnecessary variation, and supported older products retain an adequate maintenance or migration path.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_FULLER_FORM: Deprecation communication, parallel baselines, migration and revalidation of simplified products.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: End the retirement control itself when no supported product or retained obligation depends on the old variation.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION based on the source-grounded property, not a separately evaluated ceremony-removal intervention.

ceremony_stripping_ledger.ARTEFACT_RITUAL_OR_BRAND: Runtime adaptation framework, interoperable model or learned assistant
ceremony_stripping_ledger.FAILURE: Absence of configuration choices is interpreted as proof that execution is independent of environment or always predictable.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.CONSUMER: Modellers and assurance readers interpret the claim at its proper level; terminology cannot supply an unproved behavioural theorem.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.PREREQUISITES: A clear separation of configuration, ordinary input, internal state and operating environment.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.MINIMAL_ADEQUATE_ALTERNATIVE: A fixed-function program that reads a changing external value supplies a logical counterexample to the stronger inference.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.TRIGGER_FOR_FULLER_FORM: Fixed feature selection is used to infer environment-independent behaviour or a general correctness guarantee.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_SIMPLIFICATION: Simplification is inadequate if it loses this consequential postcondition: The claim is bounded to lack of configurability, without denying ordinary input/output dependence or external failure modes.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.COST_OF_FULLER_FORM: The stronger inference can create false assurance; narrowing it costs no runtime machinery.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.OMISSION_OR_RETIREMENT_CONDITION: Do not retain the broad guarantee; use ESPLE-013 and ESPLE-061 for justified early binding and reduction.
ceremony_stripping_ledger.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION based on the source-grounded property, not a separately evaluated ceremony-removal intervention.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Stable shared assumptions and recurrent product demand justify a common asset.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: Incompatible operational assumptions or incidental code similarity favour separate products or smaller common libraries.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: A narrow shared layer plus distinct product architectures.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A supposedly small shared abstraction accumulates all product exceptions and becomes the original monolith.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Future demand and coordination costs require observation, not a similarity threshold.
internal_tensions.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: explicit discriminators and hybrid risks synthesised from the linked property evidence, not a head-to-head empirical test of every hybrid.

internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_FIRST: Shared safety/interface assumptions require coordinated core decisions.
internal_tensions.CONTEXT_FAVOURING_SECOND: A local obligation has little reuse and shared generalisation would disrupt other supported products.
internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Explicit product exception on an identified baseline with shared-fix visibility.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: Every local difference becomes permanent undocumented drift, or every exception is forced back into the core.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: No universal threshold says when an exception should become a new family.
internal_tensions.EVIDENCE_STATUS: RESEARCHER_INTERPRETATION: explicit discriminators and hybrid risks synthesised from the linked property evidence, not a head-to-head empirical test of every hybrid.

internal_tensions.SUPPORTED_HYBRID: Stage investment around demonstrable commonality while retaining product delivery.
internal_tensions.HYBRID_FAILURE: A nominally incremental plan still mandates a full future platform before useful products.
internal_tensions.UNCERTAINTY: Scenario estimates should be updated from actual derivation and support costs.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 11 practitioners; 6 product lines; 3 organisations in automotive, aerospace/defence and storage.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Qualitative comparison of reasons for cloning and difficulties, not randomised economic treatment.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Documents pragmatic adoption motives, autonomy and propagation/consistency difficulties; no general causal effect estimated.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Exploratory selection, self-report and limited organisations; no representative prevalence or universal cost threshold.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Multiple observations within organisations and product lines are not independent deployments.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 10 engineers, 5 in each arm, 4 tasks each: 40 task observations, not 40 independent people; BSH setting.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Clone-and-own versus a prepared SPL implementation for the selected tasks.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Reported task-level performance favours the SPL condition in this setting. This packet does not extrapolate a universal effect or reanalyse unavailable raw data.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Small groups, repeated tasks, preparedness and excluded setup/platform investment limit transfer. Correlation/power concerns are this study’s analytical caution, not a reported retraction.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: One company/study; repeated task observations share participants and artefacts.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Historical JHipster 3.6.1; Results §6.1: 26,256 configurations, 9,376 failures (35.70%); introduction differs by one.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Exhaustive attempted configuration campaign and sampling alternatives in the reported space.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Six faults reported, including interaction order up to four; distinguishes compilation/derivation outcomes from a high-level configuration model.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: One generator/version and recorded environment; failed configurations are not independent root causes; no current prevalence claim.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Thousands of failing products share a small set of faults and the same generator.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 135 faults in the study corpus; ten sampling algorithms with varied assumptions.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Sampling strategies under different handling of headers, build information and constraints.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Relative conclusions and cost/coverage depend materially on these assumptions.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Benchmark selection, analysed languages and configuration knowledge limit transfer; fault count is not system count.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Configurable-system corpora overlap the wider analysis literature; not independent replications merely because papers differ.

empirical_evidence_register.UNITS: Analyses applied to configurable C systems
empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Seven analyses on five systems: BusyBox, OpenSSL, SQLite, Linux x86 and uClibc.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Variability-aware analysis and relevant product-oriented baselines under specified settings.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Shows scale and sharing trade-offs; outputs include warnings, not an established count of independently confirmed defects.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Underlying analyses can be imprecise; configuration/build representation and measured setups bound conclusions.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Overlaps TypeChef-related research and common open-source subjects.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Seven purposively selected diverse projects in Bosch PS-EC; mixed configuration/code-management dependencies.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Reverse-engineered variability compared and interpreted with domain knowledge.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Stale central models, heterogeneous dependencies and extraction limitations are reported; subsystem modelling is motivated.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: One family; not entire codebase; raw feature counts withheld; no controlled economic test of the proposed response.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Seven projects in one industrial programme, not seven independent industrial replications.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Three systems in one company; accessible institutional abstract only.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Field description of opportunistic reuse and variability debt.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: The abstract supports the existence of observed debt concerns, not uninspected metrics, methods or effect sizes.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Full methods, sampling and measures inaccessible; no detailed causal inference.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Possible relation to authors’ thesis/programme; no independence claim.

empirical_evidence_register.UNITS: Feature-model families, evolutions and configuration tests
empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 13 model families; 35 natural evolutions; over 3,200 mutants, as reported.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Repair/retention/regeneration alternatives for test configurations under feature-model evolution.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Demonstrates trade-offs in model/test evolution; distance-based effort proxies are not measured human maintenance labour.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Mutation and model-configuration coverage are not full behavioural defect detection; selected family corpus limits transfer.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Multiple mutants/evolutions reuse families; not thousands of independent systems.

empirical_evidence_register.UNITS: Selected software ecosystems and their variability arrangements
empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 14 selected ecosystems plus two Bitcoin-related interviews.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Taxonomic classification using project evidence and proxy measures.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Identifies independently implemented, interoperability-oriented community-driven variability as a distinct arrangement.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Researcher judgement, selection and proxy data; no causal evidence that one governance arrangement is superior.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Related 2025 precursor is ancestry, not an independent replication.

empirical_evidence_register.UNITS: Small command-line programs and historical releases
empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: 108 GNU coreutils 9.1 programs; longitudinal subset of 20 across 85 releases from 2003–2022.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Descriptive option/variability patterns and historical relations.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Supports investigation of small and earlier-bound variability; does not prove environmental independence or causal maintainability improvement.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: External libraries/build variability excluded; option counts are proxies; correlation is not causation.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Many programs share a project and releases; 2025 precursor mentioned but not independently counted.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Inspected June 2026 v1 includes ten small C/C++ examples and a wc-oriented demonstration.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Illustrative regeneration proposal, not a long-term industrial comparison against a competent maintained family.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Establishes a research proposal and examples; lifecycle superiority remains unresolved.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Small examples, changing learned models, limited continuity evidence; later HAL version blocked.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: Repeated generated examples from one proposal do not constitute independent replications.

empirical_evidence_register.SAMPLE_AND_SETTING: Ten DSLs with repeated runs, as described in the inspected preprint.
empirical_evidence_register.COMPARISON: Learned support for co-evolution of definitions and instances.
empirical_evidence_register.MEASURES_AND_OUTCOME: Useful adjacent evidence on migration assistance and validation limits; not direct SPLE family-production effectiveness.
empirical_evidence_register.UNCERTAINTY_AND_VALIDITY_THREATS: Language scale and selected tasks; repeated runs are not independent domains; transfer is a new claim.
empirical_evidence_register.DEPENDENCE: DOMAIN_TRANSLATION into SPLE, not counted as a direct industrial SPLE replication.

formal_result_register.MODEL: An explicitly encoded Boolean or richer variability model.
formal_result_register.GUARANTEE: Satisfiability and diagnostic queries concern assignments satisfying the encoded constraints.
formal_result_register.ASSUMPTIONS: Correct encoding and supported solver semantics.
formal_result_register.IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATION: Establish domain adequacy and model-to-built-product correspondence separately.

formal_result_register.MODEL: Configuration sets induced by old and new feature models and the specified correspondence.
formal_result_register.GUARANTEE: Classification of edits as specialisation, generalisation, refactoring or other set change.
formal_result_register.ASSUMPTIONS: Defined configuration semantics and correctly related features.
formal_result_register.IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATION: Feature names and configuration-set equality do not prove behavioural or requirement continuity.

formal_result_register.MODEL: Variability-aware program representation and an underlying analysis.
formal_result_register.GUARANTEE: Results retain configuration conditions and share computations; the exact claim is inherited from the underlying analysis.
formal_result_register.ASSUMPTIONS: Supported language/build/preprocessor semantics and faithful represented family.
formal_result_register.IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATION: Expose unsupported artefacts and distinguish warnings from confirmed product faults.

formal_result_register.MODEL: Discrete-event models of features, behaviour and controllable/uncontrollable events.
formal_result_register.GUARANTEE: Specified model-level safety and nonblocking through supervisory synthesis.
formal_result_register.ASSUMPTIONS: Correct plant abstraction, observable/control assumptions and feasible synthesis.
formal_result_register.IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATION: Nonblocking means a marked completion remains reachable, not that every real execution inevitably progresses; validate physical and operational correspondence.

formal_result_register.MODEL: Feature-model evolution plans, per author abstract.
formal_result_register.GUARANTEE: A modular soundness-checking approach is claimed by the abstract.
formal_result_register.ASSUMPTIONS: Full proof and precise technical assumptions were not accessible.
formal_result_register.IMPLEMENTATION_OBLIGATION: No detailed theorem or implementation guarantee is imported into this synthesis from abstract-only access.

denominator_policy: Stable ESPLE-001 through ESPLE-062. Unfavourable, ceremonial and unresolved candidates remain counted exactly once. No exact duplicate was silently removed.

population_registration_history.ACTION: Initial examined candidate families and explicit overclaims.
Retirement separated from admission because of distinct support and migration prerequisites.
Strong context-independence inference separated from the useful early-binding/null-configurability distinction.
